## Why

Seven candidate rows land as **five registry ids** after the plan's R1 consolidations: the I4-C005 MN UAV reports ride a second index target under P36.8's `statrep_mn_bca` (one source row per publisher), and the Arvada page (I4-C103) is the consolidated first target of `statrep_co_frt_accountability` (I4-C102).

## What ships

- **Five gated sources wired** (`sources.toml`, 594→592 registered — +5 design-id renames, −2 absorbed consolidation rows; 236 loadable unchanged; all `ingestion_permitted=false`, RB-03 `a` basis — Detroit RB-04 `a` — rights UNDETERMINED, `iso.3166_2` jurisdictions): `statrep_co_frt_accountability` (C.R.S. 24-18-301..-309 / SB22-113 FRT accountability family; Arvada absorbed as first target), `statrep_wa_watech_frt` (RCW 43.386 TSB posting of NOI + accountability reports), `statrep_detroit_mi_frt_weekly` (DPD Directive 307.5-5.1 weekly FRT reports to the BOPC), `statrep_me_dps_uav` (25 M.R.S. § 4501 annual UAV-use report), `statrep_il_icjia_drone` (725 ILCS 167 SFY publications index). The generated `statrep_co_arvada_facial_recognition` and `statrep_mn_unmanned_aerial_vehicle` rows are absorbed (deleted) under the R1 consolidation; their `promote` disposition placeholders resolve with the renamed rows (connector-mapped sources carry no disposition row).
- **Targets** (`live_targets.toml`): `statrep_mn_bca` gains the `uav_annual_reports` index target (`doc_url_contains=uav`, `.pdf` only, max 8); CO ×1, WaTech ×1, Detroit ×1, ICJIA ×1 `index_page` targets; Maine ×1 `disclosure_document` — all bounded (`max_documents` ≤ 12, same-host + path/suffix filters).
- **Vocab** (`government_mandated_disclosure_vocab.toml`, `vocab_version 2026.10.13`): five `[sources]` keys → the I8 §5.6 design ids; eight FRT/UAV spellings join `[technology_map]` (`facial rec`, `frs`, `facial recognition system/technology`, `drone surveillance`, plural UAS/UAV/unmanned forms → `face-recognition-unspecified`/`uas-unspecified`); five reviewed `[adapters.<publisher>]` specs — Detroit is `reports_use = true` with `usage_count` `use_fields` only (per-week aggregates, never per-incident), ICJIA runs `document_entries` agency rows as `reported_owned` `inventory_entry` assertions (ownership ≠ deployment — no use claims), WaTech's `reports_use_pattern` admits accountability reports only (an NOI is a pre-deployment declaration), Maine carries the § 4501 statewide aggregate literal.
- **Shared-adapter guard** (`government_mandated_disclosure.py`): `ordinance_literal_required` — a source covering several statutory mandates (MN BCA carries the § 13.824 LPR list AND the § 626.19 UAV reports) must not stamp the source-level citation on a filing that never names it; the flag emits the `ordinance` claim only where an ordinance literal is located in the filing's own text (the UAV filing's own § 626.19 lands as `legal_authority`). Without the flag the historical fallback emit stands — diff 0 for every P36.8 adapter. Also: `unmapped_technology_literals` now propagates onto the emitted artifact row (P36.8 set the field but never carried it downstream — the SIG-ONTO-021 refusal is now visible on the artifact).
- **MN BCA adapter extension** (`[adapters.mn_bca]`): per-agency `— N UAV uses` entry rows (`reported_uav_use`, typed `uas-unspecified`), `technology_field_pattern`/`technology_anchor_pattern` covering the UAV literals (a filing's own `Technology:` field types it — never the LPR default), `legal_authority_pattern` for 13.824/626.19, the statewide `usage_count` use field, `document_entries`, `ordinance_literal_required`.
- **Cadence** (`ops/cadence.toml`): `r11-disclosures-02` membership updated to the five design ids; the two absorbed generated seats are removed (`statrep_mn_bca` keeps its disclosures-01 seat — a source holds one batch seat); the P36.9b members unchanged; still create-paused (R6), lint-clean.
- **Fixtures + tests**: eleven synthetic reconstructions under `tests/connectors/fixtures/statrep/` with `SOURCES.md` provenance (index pages exercising same-host/path-fan-out and the scope/path screens — the WaTech `biometric` NOI exercises the unmapped-literal path, the ICJIA firearms filing + `icjia.state.il.us` mirror exercise the path/host filters, the Detroit agenda PDF exercises the `facial` filter, the MN `lrl.mn.gov` mirror exercises the same-host rule; plaintext filings exercising field/use literals). `tests/connectors/test_statrep_p36_9a.py` (34 tests): registration/routing/gating, live-target kinds, cadence membership, adapter claim shapes per publisher, Detroit `disclosure_use`-only weekly counts with no per-incident field, ICJIA ownership assertions, the `ordinance_literal_required` guard on the shared MN row, unmapped-literal recording, the aggregate schema on every emitted row, fixture provenance, and +0 shadow replay.
- **`test_review_status.py`**: the two registry-count assertions updated for the consolidation (594 → 592 — the generated-count comments re-explained); no living-record pins added (OM-15).
